n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, photographs showing people with expansive postures received a higher average rating of trait dominance (m = 3.738, sd = 0.614; n = 233) on the eight-item social dominance subscale measured on 5-point Likert scales compared to photos showing people with contracted postures (m = 2.904, sd = 1.054; n = 217). The difference in the average ratings of 0.833 was tested using an independent samples t-test with equal variances (t(448) = 10.334, p < 0.001; n = 450). As a result, we can reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the trait dominance rating between contracted postures photographs and expansive postures photographs. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 0.974 (95% CI [0.789, 1.160]).
